data: First Soyuz generation; Komarov's fatal flight
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Soyuz 1 (1967-04-23) · Vladimir Komarov — FATAL: parachute tangled at landing after 18 orbits of attitude-control failures; first in-flight cosmonaut death
Soyuz 3 (1968-10-26) · Georgy Beregovoy — first Soviet flight after Komarov; attempted rendezvous with uncrewed Soyuz 2 (overshot)
Soyuz 4 (1969-01-14) · Vladimir Shatalov — docked with Soyuz 5; first crew transfer between two crewed spacecraft (via EVA)
Soyuz 5 (1969-01-15) · Volynov + Khrunov + Yeliseyev — Khrunov + Yeliseyev EVA-transferred to Soyuz 4; Volynov returned solo with descent module separation failure (survived)
Soyuz 9 (1970-06-01) · Nikolayev + Sevastyanov — 18-day endurance flight; longest crewed flight to date; informed Salyut programme design
Soyuz 11 (1971-06-06) · Dobrovolsky + Volkov + Patsayev — Salyut 1 first crew (23 days); FATAL: cabin depressurised at separation; crew killed

The Soyuz 7K-OK was the first of the line — the original version of the spacecraft that would outlive them all. It introduced the three-module layout every Soyuz since has kept: a spherical orbital module to live and work in, a compact descent module to ride home in, and a service module for power and propulsion. It was also the version that killed Vladimir Komarov on its first crewed flight and, in an improved form, the three cosmonauts of Soyuz 11 — the hard early schooling that turned a rushed design into a reliable one. Crude and dangerous at the start, its basic architecture proved so sound that, refined over decades, it is still carrying crews to orbit today.

The first generation of Soyuz, with all the architectural choices that have endured for sixty years: orbital module sphere, descent module, service module with deployable solar arrays. Tragically introduced by Soyuz 1 (Komarov’s fatal flight, 1967).
First crewed Soyuz flight — parachute failure killed Vladimir Komarov (first in-flight spaceflight death)
First crew to a space station (Salyut 1); all 3 died of decompression on reentry
First international human spaceflight cooperation; first US-USSR rendezvous + docking
R-7-derived launcher for the first-generation Soyuz spacecraft — flew Soyuz 1 (1967) and Soyuz 11 (1971)
Sputnik 1 (1957). Vostok 1 — Gagarin (1961). Five hundred and forty Soyuz launches from a single pad.
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
Apollo 10 + Skylab + 53 Shuttle flights; now NASA's SLS / Artemis pad
Buran's atmospheric analog — equivalent of NASA's Enterprise. Four jet engines, 24 atmospheric tests 1985-88, never to orbit
Soviet shuttle; one unmanned flight, never crewed
